1.4.0 on 4215 (Vasily-X; package-metadata has no issues URL). A 7 KB plugin that persists code folds per file: storage is Packages/User/AutoFoldCode.sublime-settings as {version, folds: {path: {content-crc32-hex: [[start, end], ...]}}, selections}, with max_buffer_size 1000000 and save_selections true; four commands (auto_fold_code_clear_all "Clear All", auto_fold_code_clear_current "Clear Current File", auto_fold_code_unfold_all "Unfold All Open Files", plus the internal auto_fold_code_restore) and an Open Settings entry. WORKS end to end: folding a demo.py (fold_by_level level 2, region rows 1-4) and saving wrote the storage file with the absolute path keyed by "0xb0ae41c8" (CRC32 of the content) and the region as character offsets [29, 99]; closing and reopening the file restored exactly that fold (view.folded_regions() = ((1,16),(4,24))). auto_fold_code_clear_current on the window unfolded the view and the reopened file then had no folds, and auto_fold_code_unfold_all cleared the live folds - so clear and unfold both do their job. Folds are keyed by content CRC32, so an edited file simply stops matching its stored folds, which is the documented intent (on_post_save keeps only the latest version). WART, recorded not filed: clearing does not remove the entry from the settings file - after both clear_current and clear_all the saved file still contains the old block, wrapped in /* ... */, and each cleared file leaves another commented block behind. Logically it is inert (it is a comment, and my reopen confirmed nothing was restored) but the file accumulates dead data; _clear_cache just pops the key and calls sublime.save_settings, so the comment is produced by the save path rather than by design. ALSO: clear_current/clear_all are WindowCommands - view.run_command(...) silently does nothing for them; they have to be invoked on the window (worth knowing when scripting this plugin). Installed through the picker, "reloading plugin AutoOpenReadme.AutoOpenReadme" with no traceback, no dialog. Each claim proved in a real new window (the plugin keys on the window, so every case needs its own window opened with the portable's own "sublime_text.exe -n <folder>", which is how a person opens a folder in a new window): (1) root beats docs - folder with both readme.md and docs/readme.md opened readme.md, matching the README's rule that folders are searched in order and each is checked for every filename before moving on; (2) deeper folder alone - a folder whose only candidate was docs/notes.txt opened docs/notes.txt; (3) per-folder override - .sublime.autoopen listing todo.md then readme.md opened exactly those two tabs in that order and skipped the defaults, and the "# ..." comment line in that file was ignored; (4) case - README.MD was opened against the shipped "readme.md" entry, as the README says it does on Windows; (5) nothing to open - a folder with only code.py opened no file, left the window untitled and printed no error; (6) multi-folder - one window with two folders, each holding its own .sublime.autoopen, opened c/todo.md, c/readme.md and f/notes2.md, so the override really is per folder as documented; (7) configurability - a User AutoOpenReadme.sublime-settings with "files": ["notes.txt", "readme.md"] made notes.txt win over readme.md in a folder holding both, without a restart, so the setting is read live from settings() on every event. No defect found, nothing filed. Observations recorded, not filed because neither changes what a user sees: comment lines in .sublime.autoopen whose first character is whitespace are turned into candidate filenames (the "#" test runs before the strip, so " # x" becomes "# x" and is then skipped for not existing), and window_markers is never pruned, so a long-lived editor holds one window id string per window it has ever had. Two behaviours worth the record: (1) NATIVE MODALS ON THE MAIN THREAD. When <question>_Default.<ext> already exists, cp_new raises "... already exists. Do you want to override the old file?" (Yes/Cancel); cp_open on a question with no file raises "... does not exist. Do you want to create ...?". Both block Sublime itself: every sublime-mcp route then times out after 5 s (eval_python: "A native window blocks Sublime's main thread until it is dismissed"), which is exactly what a frozen editor looks like from outside. list_native_windows still answers while blocked and returns the dialog text and buttons, and dismiss_native_window {"hwnd": ..., "action": "button", "button": "Yes"} closes it with no focus change. (2) DETECTION. These pickers are invisible to get_quick_panel (the plugin loads in the 3.14 host, and only the 3.8/3.3 hosts record panels) and invisible to the accessibility tree; only a window screenshot shows them. Posted Return frequently does nothing unless the window is in front, and often needs a second press. cp_end afterwards restored one pane, minimap on and an empty build system, so the layout changes are reversible. Verdict: works, with the blocking-modal caveat. Scope reads are correct for the dialect-aware design: '\ line comment' -> comment.line.forth with punctuation.definition.comment.forth; a '(' alone at end of line opens comment.block.forth and the matching ')' closes it with punctuation.definition.comment.end.forth; ': square' -> meta.colon.forth meta.declaration.forth, calls like 'square'/'dup' -> variable.other.forth, 'variable' -> keyword.declaration.forth, '." hello world"' -> string.quoted.double.forth, numbers -> constant.numeric.decimal.forth. Design point worth knowing, not a defect: an INLINE '( n -- n*n )' is scoped markup.raw.forth with the words inside as variable.other.forth, because the syntax models parens content as stack-effect params; only '(' at end of line becomes a comment block. The tmPreferences define both styles (TM_COMMENT_START '\ ' and START_2/END_2 '(' / ')'), and toggle_comment on '42 square .' produced '\ 42 square .' and restored it. Test discipline: console marker 128 taken before the install; afterwards 0 new console lines with no error lines; no dialogs; the quick panel reported 'none is open'; views, project folder and panels cleared before the row. LOADS AND ATTACHES, tsserver bridge dead on 0.6.1 - LSP-ember 0.6.1 (2026-10-15), ST4 4215 / Python 3.14.6. Step 0 first: ijlee2/LSP-ember is active (pushed 2026-11-02), issues enabled with zero open issues and one open PR (#17, from rchl, "Registered @glint/tsserver-plugin with LSP-typescript on start"), not in data\do_not_file.tsv - and #17 turned out to be the answer to what I saw, so nothing was filed. Installed the five packages the README names (Handlebars 2026.07.16, LSP 2.16.0 with its five libraries, LSP-ember 0.6.1, LSP-typescript 3.2.5, Template Tag 4.0.1), all through the Package Control picker, then restarted as the README requires. What works: every package installs and reloads with no traceback ("reloading plugin LSP-ember.plugin"), a .gts file gets "Glimmer TS" from Template Tag (source.gts, so the client's selector can match at all - without Template Tag the file is Plain Text and nothing attaches), the package provisions its own server (npm installed 49 packages into Data\Package Storage\LSP-ember\server-4e272ad0, @glint/ember-tsc 1.11.6), the status bar reads "LSP: ember | typescript (6.0.3, bundled)", and a real Glint-shaped project (package.json with @glint/core, @glint/tsserver-plugin and @glint/environment-ember-template-imports, tsconfig with the tsserver plugin, app/components/demo.gts with a Signature declaring only "name") opens and is served by the client. What does not work: on every start the console prints "[LSP-ember] LSP-typescript not found, or it has not loaded @glint/tsserver-plugin. Try restarting Sublime Text." (reproduced on three restarts), and the deliberate template error I put in demo.gts - "{{@typoArg}}" against a Signature that declares only "name" - produces no diagnostic at all. Control for the rig: a plain TypeScript type error (const x: number = "not a number") in the same project DID get a red gutter dot and underline from LSP-typescript, so the rig does surface diagnostics; the .gts file gets none because plain tsserver cannot check a template and Glint's tsserver half is the part that never registered. Cause is in the shipped code and matches PR #17's own description: 0.6.1 still points LSP-typescript at ${storage_path}/LSP-ember/server/node_modules/ through typescript-plugins.json, while lsp_utils 4.0 installs the server into the hashed server-4e272ad0 directory (observed here), so @glint/tsserver-plugin is never loaded; the PR replaces that with LSP-typescript 3.2.5's lsp_typescript_register_plugin command. So the release installs, loads, provisions and attaches, but cannot report a template error until that PR lands - recorded rather than filed, because filing would duplicate the open PR. Not filed, and no patch made. Probe used and removed: a User/LSP-typescript.sublime-settings that added source.gts and source.gjs to LSP-typescript's shipped selector (source.js, source.jsx, source.ts, source.tsx) so a tsserver session for a .gts file could exist at all; the console message and the missing diagnostic were identical with and without it.

Measured directly on a four-line .asm: a section TYPE token gets only 'source.rgbds storage.type.section.rgbds' both in SECTION (ROM0 line 1, HRAM line 2) and in LOAD (HRAM line 3), while the attribute tokens do get their wrapper (BANK and ALIGN line 3 -> 'meta.annotation.parameters.section-attrs.rgbds storage.modifier.rgbds'), and the quoted section name does get 'meta.annotation.parameters.section-type.rgbds'. So the package's own expectation is right and the unquoted section-type branch is missing the meta scope. Second finding while measuring: 'LOAD "Other", ROM0[$200]' scopes ROM0 as 'invalid.illegal.rgbds', i.e. the syntax underlines legal RGBDS (LOAD accepts ROM section types) as illegal. 2018.12.26.20.58.56 on 4215 (mcw0933; no issues URL). A one-class SublimeLinter linter: TerraformLinter with cmd "tflint $file_on_disk", selector source.terraform, tempfile_suffix "-", and a single output regex. NEEDS TWO THINGS IT DOES NOT DECLARE. First SublimeLinter: on install with only Package Control's baseline the plugin dies at import with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'SublimeLinter' (linter.py line 2) - there is no dependency declaration and no message telling the user, so it just silently does nothing. Installing SublimeLinter by hand made the module load (SublimeLinter-contrib-tflint then appears in sys.modules with its linter submodule and TerraformLinter subclassing SublimeLinter.lint.Linter). Second a Terraform syntax package: the selector is source.terraform, which stock Sublime does not provide. And of course the tflint binary itself - not on this rig, so no real lint run was possible. THE OUTPUT REGEX IS FOR A TFLINT THAT NO LONGER EXISTS, verified against tflint's own printer sources rather than guessed: it is r'^.+?(?:(?P<error>ERROR)|(?P<warning>WARNING|NOTICE)):(?P<line>\d+) (?P<message>.+)'. That matches tflint's old default printer exactly - I ran it against the format string from printer/default.go at v0.7.0 (a tab, then "ERROR:1 message (detector)") and it parsed ERROR:1, WARNING:3 and NOTICE:10 correctly.
